haiku-low.q1: It still works. Accounts are found by Google sub, not email, so the same account gets a session. The changed email is not used or stored.
haiku-low.q2: The email must be verified. The user must then enter that account's password at the confirm page, which creates the link. Only then does start_session run.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. At 5, locked_until is set 15 minutes ahead, the counter resets to 0, and the link record and cookie are deleted.
haiku-low.q4: A new users row (no password, email verified now) and a google_identities row are created in one transaction, then the user is signed in. If unverified, the login page asks for email and password first; nothing is created.
haiku-low.q5: Both cases show an error page and change nothing. After 12 minutes the txn has expired. A second load finds it already used by GETDEL.
haiku-low.q6: It runs start_session: the old sessions row for the browser's sid is deleted, a new row is inserted, and a new sid cookie is set. The old sid is replaced, not kept.
haiku-low.q7: No password or email match is required, only a valid sid matching the txn hash. If the Google account belongs to another user, or this user has a different Google account, the link is refused.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis at gauth:txn:{state} with a 600 s TTL. It holds nonce, PKCE verifier, entry, next, and for settings user_id and sid hash. GETDEL at callback or TTL expiry removes it.
haiku-low.q9: In Redis at gauth:link:{id} (TTL 600 s), holding sub, user_id and next. The browser refers to it by the gauth_link cookie holding the id. Success, lockout, cancel, refused check or TTL expiry deletes it.
haiku-low.q10: In the google_identities table. sub is the primary key, so one Google account links to one user. user_id is unique, so one user has one Google account.
haiku-low.q11: The user returns to the page the flow began on with: Google sign-in did not finish. Try again, or use email and password. Details go to server logs. The exchange is not retried, since the txn is used.
haiku-low.q12: The txn's entry field (login or settings) tells the callback which branch to run. Settings checks the sid hash and links to the stored user_id. Login matches the lowercased email and needs password confirmation.

sonnet.q1: Nothing breaks. Accounts are identified by sub, not email. A linked sub goes straight to start_session(user_id), so the changed Google email still reaches the same account.
sonnet.q2: The user must confirm the account password. The callback saves a link record (gauth:link:{id}, TTL 600 s, holding sub, user_id and next) and sets the gauth_link cookie. It then 303-redirects to the password prompt at /auth/google/confirm. A right password inside the DB transaction commits the google_identities row, sets failed_logins to 0 and sets email_verified_at if it is NULL. Then start_session runs. This holds only if that user has no different Google account, and sub is not linked to another user.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. At 5, locked_until is set to now plus 15 minutes and failed_logins resets to 0. The link record and gauth_link cookie are deleted. The user lands on the login page with 'Account temporarily locked.' Nothing is linked. Before that, the form shows again with 'Wrong password.' The 10 minutes are not extended.
sonnet.q4: Verified email and no matching user: one DB transaction inserts a users row (password_hash NULL, email_verified_at now) and a google_identities row. Then start_session runs and the user is signed in as a new user. Email not verified: the login page says to verify with email and password first, and nothing is created.
sonnet.q5: Both cases fail the same way. The txn is gone (the Redis TTL of 600 s expired, or GETDEL already used it), so the callback shows the error page. Nothing changes, the gauth_txn cookie is cleared, and no GETDEL runs.
sonnet.q6: start_session(user_id) creates the same session as password login. It inserts a new sessions row, sets the sid cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax) and redirects to next if it is a relative path on our site, otherwise to /home. It deletes the sessions row of any sid the browser already sent, so the old session is replaced, not kept.
sonnet.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required. Settings entry needs only a valid sid. The email is not compared or stored. If the sub is already linked to another user, the link is refused with a message on the Settings page, and nothing changes. It is also refused if this user already has a different Google account.
sonnet.q8: They are kept in the Redis txn record gauth:txn:{state} (TTL 600 s). The txn also holds entry, next and, for settings only, user_id and the sid hash. The browser holds the state in the gauth_txn cookie. GETDEL at the callback removes the txn (single use), or the TTL expires it. The gauth_txn cookie is cleared on every callback response, or it expires after Max-Age 600 s.
sonnet.q9: It is held in the Redis record gauth:link:{id} (sub, user_id, next; TTL 600 s). The browser refers to it with the gauth_link cookie holding the id (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/auth/google). It is deleted on success after the commit, on lockout, on Cancel (POST /auth/google/cancel), on a refused commit check, or by TTL expiry. A failed DB commit keeps it until the TTL.
sonnet.q10: The new google_identities table (sub, user_id, linked_at). sub is the PRIMARY KEY, so one Google account links to at most one user. user_id is NOT NULL UNIQUE (REFERENCES users ON DELETE CASCADE), so one user has at most one Google account.
sonnet.q11: The user goes back to the page the flow began on with 'Google sign-in did not finish. Try again, or use email and password.' There is no retry: the txn is already used (GETDEL), so the code cannot be retried and the user must start again. Nothing changes. Details go to server logs only.
sonnet.q12: The entry value (login or settings) is saved in the txn at start, and the callback branches on it. For settings, the txn stores user_id and the SHA-256 hash of the sid. The callback checks that the hash of the current sid cookie equals the txn's hash and that the sessions row is still live. If not, the user goes to the login page with 'Please sign in again' and nothing changes. This stops a link started with an attacker's Google account from being attached to the victim.
